status: Closed — runner publication deletion and governed takeover re-verified 2026-09-02
finding: Runner-sync publication can deadlock after a clean build deletes stale release artifacts: the sealed output inventory enumerates existing runner outputs but omits deletion entries, so runner-sync release classifies those deleted publication paths as extra output and returns ATM_RUNNER_PUBLICATION_INVENTORY_INCOMPLETE. The ATM git emergency wrapper also checks task write-ticket scope before honoring hook-bypass approval, so it cannot commit the runner publication surfaces that runner-sync itself requires.
expectedBehavior: Runner-sync inventory should model create, modify, and delete publication operations as first-class sealed members, and the governed emergency path should either consume a runner-sync/steward publication lease or fail with a specific runner-publication-scope error plus a bounded recovery command.
evidenceOrRepro: Historical reproduction: ATM-GOV-0244 runner-sync receipt omitted five deleted release/atm-root-drop *.d.ts paths, then runner-sync release returned ATM_RUNNER_PUBLICATION_INVENTORY_INCOMPLETE and the governed commit seam refused the publication surfaces. Current source re-verification on 2026-09-02: runner-build-output-inventory fingerprints tracked pre-build members as `missing` after deletion and includes them in the sealed inventory; digest-bound takeover plans explicitly preserve `missing` as an observed state. `runner-publication-inventory-parity`, `runner-publication-disposition-gate`, `runner-sync-steward-release`, `runner-sync-framework-temp-hotfix`, and `runner-sync-foreign-dirty-owner` all passed. The framework-temp claim plus queue-head runner-sync publication path was also exercised in the current repository without raw git or emergency bypass.
followUp: Closed. Keep the deletion/takeover regression tests in the runner-sync validation surface; any future failure must reopen this item with a new sealed reproduction rather than relying on the 2026-07-29 receipt.
